title: Evaluation on retracts and extension of a perfect pairing
statement:
Rational evaluation and biduality restrict to split idempotents.
If a pairing $b:K\otimes L\to\omega$ has isomorphisms as
both adjoints $K\to DL$ and $L\to DK$, and idempotents
on its two factors are adjoint under $b$, its restriction to
their images again has both adjoints isomorphisms. This property
is preserved by finite scalar extension. In particular it holds
for Verdier evaluation $DK\otimes K\to\omega$ and its
retracts. For a site-perfect complex, the usual perfect pairing
with its tensor dual to the coefficient unit also restricts and
extends in this way.

proof.text: Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, exactly as in [thm-coef-rational-verdier]. Take the finite coefficient fields inside the fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of the coefficient conventions, as required by [lem-weil-rationalization-idempotent-complete]. Work in the rationalized category $\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(X,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with the tensor and internal Hom of [lem-coef-rational-operations]. Write $D=R\mathcal Hom_E(-,\omega_{X,E})$. The evaluation-defined natural maps $\delta_A:A\to D^2A$ are isomorphisms by [thm-coef-rational-verdier]. By [lem-weil-rationalization-idempotent-complete], idempotents split inside this very category. Thus choose splittings $P\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{p}P$ and $Q\xrightarrow{j}L\xrightarrow{q}Q$ with $pi=1_P$, $qj=1_Q$, $ip=e$ and $jq=f$. Here and below compositions are written in ordinary right-to-left order. The argument below works for any chosen splittings; it does not adjoin objects to the rationalized category.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 1 and 3: rational duality and the existing splittings

proof.text: Contravariance gives $D(j)D(q)=1_{DQ}$ and $D(q)D(j)=D(f)$, and similarly $D(i)D(p)=1_{DP}$ and $D(p)D(i)=D(e)$. Let $a:K\xrightarrow{\sim}DL$ and $c:L\xrightarrow{\sim}DK$ be the two adjoints of $b$. The hypothesis that the idempotents are adjoint is the equation $b(e\otimes1_L)=b(1_K\otimes f)$. Transposition in the tensor–Hom adjunction turns it into $ae=D(f)a$ and $cf=D(e)c$. Define $b_{P,Q}=b(i\otimes j):P\otimes Q\to\omega$. Naturality of that same adjunction says that its adjoints are exactly $a'=D(j)ai:P\to DQ$ and $c'=D(i)cj:Q\to DP$: precomposing either input of a pairing precomposes the corresponding input of its transpose, contravariantly on the internal-Hom variable.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: transposes of the restricted pairing, written explicitly

proof.text:
The inverse of $a'$ is $p a^{-1}D(q)$. Indeed,
$$
(p a^{-1}D(q))(D(j)ai)=p a^{-1}D(f)ai=pei=1_P,
$$
$$
(D(j)ai)(p a^{-1}D(q))=D(j)ae a^{-1}D(q)=D(j)D(f)D(q)=1_{DQ}.
$$
The last equality uses $D(j)D(f)D(q)=D(qfj)=D(1_Q)$. For the second adjoint put $s=q c^{-1}D(p)$. Its inverse equations are
$$
s c'=q c^{-1}D(p)D(i)cj=q c^{-1}D(e)cj=qfj=1_Q,
$$
$$
c's=D(i)cjq c^{-1}D(p)=D(i)cf c^{-1}D(p)=D(i)D(e)D(p)=D(pei)=1_{DP}.
$$ Thus both adjoints of the restricted pairing are isomorphisms. This proves the general assertion by actual inverse maps, including zero idempotents; it uses neither an image theorem nor preservation of kernels.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: why the induced maps on images are isomorphisms

proof.text:
For a retract $P\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{p}P$, put $h=ip$. The splitting of $D(h)$ is $DP\xrightarrow{D(p)}DK\xrightarrow{D(i)}DP$. Evaluation naturality is
$$
\mathrm{ev}_K(D(p)\otimes1_K)=\mathrm{ev}_P(1_{DP}\otimes p).
$$
Precompose with $1_{DP}\otimes i$ and use $pi=1_P$ to get
$$
\mathrm{ev}_K(D(p)\otimes i)=\mathrm{ev}_P.
$$
The two adjoints of $\mathrm{ev}_K:DK\otimes K\to\omega$ are $1_{DK}$ and $\delta_K$, so they are isomorphisms by [thm-coef-rational-verdier]. The same naturality equation, with $p$ replaced by $h$, proves that $D(h)$ and $h$ are adjoint. Finally naturality of the biduality in that cited theorem gives
$$
\delta_P=D^2(p)\,\delta_K\,i.
$$
Its inverse is $p\,\delta_K^{-1}\,D^2(i)$: the two products reduce to identities using $pi=1_P$ and $D^2(h)\delta_K=\delta_K h$. This proves restriction of the actual evaluation and actual biduality maps, not just existence of an unspecified perfect pairing on $P$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1 and first sentence of paragraph 2: evaluation and natural biduality on a summand

proof.text:
For a finite extension $E\subset F$, let $T=-\otimes_EF$ be [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. The tensor comparison is the rational image of the completed-tensor comparison in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]; the dualizing-object comparison $u:T\omega_{X,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,F}$ is the rational image of $u_{F/E}$ in [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension]. These are comparisons for the prescribed integral-representative scalar extension, rather than tensoring an arbitrary discrete sheaf by a topological field. Write $c_{A,B}:TA\otimes_FTB\xrightarrow{\sim}T(A\otimes_EB)$ for the inverse of the rationalized tensor comparison. The evaluation compatibility supplied by [thm-coef-rational-verdier] is $\mathrm{ev}_{F,TA}(\beta_A\otimes1_{TA})=uT(\mathrm{ev}_{E,A})c_{DA,A}$. Define $b_F=uT(b)c_{K,L}$. By the evaluation compatibility in [thm-coef-rational-verdier], its first adjoint is
$$
a_F=\beta_L\,T(a):TK\longrightarrow D_F(TL),
$$
where $\beta_A:T(DA)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_F(TA)$ is that theorem's comparison; the second is $c_F=\beta_KT(c)$. Their inverses are $T(a^{-1})\beta_L^{-1}$ and $T(c^{-1})\beta_K^{-1}$. Applying $T$ to $pi=1$, $qj=1$, $ip=e$, $jq=f$, and the adjoint-idempotent equation gives splittings and adjoint idempotents after extension. Naturality gives $\beta_Q T(D(j))=D_F(Tj)\beta_L$ (and $\beta_L T(D(q))=D_F(Tq)\beta_Q$, with the analogous equations for $i,p$), so the restricted transpose $\beta_QT(a')$ is exactly $D_F(Tj)a_F(Ti)$. Consequently the inverse formulas of step 3 are carried to the inverse formulas over $F$. The biduality compatibility in [thm-coef-rational-verdier] is $\beta_{DA}T(\delta_{E,A})=D_F(\beta_A)\delta_{F,TA}$, an equality of maps $TA\to D_F(TDA)$. Applying this equality to the maps in step 4, together with the displayed naturality equations, carries its retract identity for biduality to the identity over $F$. Only functoriality is needed to preserve inverse maps; no reflection of isomorphisms is being assumed.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: the finite scalar-extension comparison and its effect on every displayed map

proof.text: For the last clause let $A$ be site-perfect as in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], put $B=A^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_E(A,\mathbf1_E)$, and let $b:B\otimes A\to\mathbf1_E$ be its usual evaluation. These are the coefficient-passage internal Hom and evaluation of [lem-coef-rational-operations], not a discrete constant-field construction. Let $d_A:A\to A^{\vee\vee}$ be the transpose of $b$ with the inputs interchanged. The two adjoints of $b$ are $1_B$ and $d_A$, so it suffices to prove the latter invertible. We prove this locally and then justify detection in the raw scalar localization explicitly. Derived internal Hom commutes with slice restriction and is exact in either argument by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]; these identities rationalize, since the rational internal Hom is the integral operation on objects and the scalar-localized operation on morphisms. Exact restriction of sheaves is [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. For completed tensor, restrict its defining finite-level K-flat models and its Roos complex: restrictions of the K-flat models remain K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], restriction commutes with sectionwise products, and hence with the finite cone matrices. Sectionwise exact products are supplied by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Thus the completed tensor, evaluation, its transpose $d_A$, and their rational images restrict to the corresponding operations on the slice. This establishes restriction of the actual canonical map, without assuming a six-functor datum.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: define the usual coefficient dual and restrict the actual maps; Stacks 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U) for ordinary internal Hom, with completed/rational passage expanded here

proof.text:
On a chosen slice where $A$ has a bounded finite-projective model $P$ in degrees $[a,b]$, consider the coefficient dual $V\mapsto V^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_E(V,\mathbf1_E)$. It is contravariantly exact, including the signed shift identifications, by the ringed-Hom exactness theorem and scalar localization. Its square is covariantly exact. The evaluation-defined $d_V$ is a morphism between their triangles: on Hom complexes the dual differential is $d_{V^\vee}^r(\phi)=(-1)^{r+1}\phi d_V^{-r-1}$ and double evaluation in degree $r$ is $x\mapsto(\phi\mapsto(-1)^r\phi(x))$; substituting in this differential verifies the chain-map equation and the shifted cone-square signs. These equations survive deriving and rationalizing, since the coefficient comparisons preserve evaluation. Hence the objects where $d_V$ is invertible are closed under shifts and triangles by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso]. They contain the unit, since $R\mathcal Hom_E(\mathbf1_E,-)$ is the identity under the unit adjunction, and therefore contain its finite sums. They are closed under retracts: if $V\xrightarrow{i}W\xrightarrow{p}V$ has $pi=1$, naturality gives $d_V=(p^{\vee\vee})d_Wi$, with inverse $p d_W^{-1}(i^{\vee\vee})$; the products are identities by $pi=1$ and $d_Wip=(ip)^{\vee\vee}d_W$. Each $P^r$ is such a retract by the site-perfect definition. Starting with $\sigma_{\geq b+1}P=0$, descend through the degreewise split cone triangles
$$\sigma_{\geq r+1}P\longrightarrow\sigma_{\geq r}P\longrightarrow P^r[-r]\longrightarrow(\sigma_{\geq r+1}P)[1].$$
The third term is in this class, so two-out-of-three puts the middle term in the class. This finite induction proves that $d_A$ is invertible on the chosen slice. Dualizing the finite local model reverses the degrees and dualizes each finite-free retraction, so its coefficient dual also has a bounded local model of finite projective terms, with the displayed dual differential. This uses the rational local models themselves and does not assume they lift to integral perfect lattices.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: local finite-free/retract and bounded-complex biduality; Stacks 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), expanded via finite cone triangles at the rational stage

proof.text: To pass from this local calculation to the raw rational category, choose integral representatives for the endpoints of $d_A$ and write that rational morphism as an integral numerator divided by $\varpi_E^t$. Let $C$ be the integral cone of its numerator. The integral endpoints and their cone belong to $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by the coefficient-operation domains and [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]; its rational image is a cone of $d_A$ up to the invertible scalar. The finite-type definition gives a finite affine open cover of $X$. On each affine the pro-etale covering definition refines the site-perfect cover by finitely many affine opens in its members. Collect them to obtain a finite covering $\{U_j\to X\}_{j=1}^s$ where step 7 applies. If $X$ is empty, every sheaf is zero and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, exact restriction shows that $C|_{U_j}$ is zero in the scalar localization. By the Hom-module definition of that localization, the image of $\operatorname{id}_{C|_{U_j}}$ in $\operatorname{End}(C|_{U_j})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ is zero. The tensor-localization isomorphism and the localization equivalence relation give $\varpi_E^{N_j}\operatorname{id}_{C|_{U_j}}=0$ for some $N_j\geq0$. Let $N=\max_jN_j$. Exact restriction identifies the restrictions of $\varpi_E^N H^r(C)$ with zero maps for every $r$. A section therefore restricts to zero on a covering, so the separatedness axiom for a sheaf makes it zero. Thus $\varpi_E^N H^r(C)=0$ globally for every $r$. This is a statement about cohomology; it has not yet asserted that the same scalar kills $\operatorname{id}_C$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: global detection after rational local calculations; finite-cover and uniform-denominator argument supplied here

proof.text: The integral cone $C$ has bounded cohomology. Indeed its reductions have support in one interval $[u,v]$ by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. In its Roos triangle from [def-weil-derived-complete], exact countable products have cohomology only in $[u,v]$. The long exact sequence therefore places $H^r(C)$ in $[u,v+1]$. In any distinguished triangle $A_0\xrightarrow{i}B_0\xrightarrow{p}D_0\to A_0[1]$, suppose $\varpi_E^e\operatorname{id}_{A_0}=0$ and $\varpi_E^f\operatorname{id}_{D_0}=0$. Then $p\varpi_E^f=\varpi_E^fp=0$, so exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(B_0,-)$ gives $\varpi_E^f\operatorname{id}_{B_0}=ih$ for some $h:B_0\to A_0$. Multiply by $\varpi_E^e$ to obtain $\varpi_E^{e+f}\operatorname{id}_{B_0}=0$. Apply this to the canonical truncation triangles of $C$, starting with $\tau_{\leq u-1}C=0$ and adjoining $H^r(C)[-r]$ for $u\leq r\leq v+1$. Step 8 says each of these successive pieces is killed by $\varpi_E^N$, so induction gives $\varpi_E^{N(v-u+2)}\operatorname{id}_C=0$. The last truncation is isomorphic to $C$ because its other cohomology vanishes. After scalar localization $\varpi_E$ is invertible, hence $\operatorname{id}_C=0$ and $C=0$. Thus $d_A$ is an isomorphism globally. The two adjoints $1_B,d_A$ show that the usual unit-valued evaluation has precisely the perfection asserted in the statement.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: bounded-cohomology truncation argument completing global rational detection

proof.text: For a unit-valued pairing with adjoints $a:K\xrightarrow{\sim}L^\vee$ and $c:L\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee$, its restriction along splittings $i,p,j,q$ has adjoints $j^\vee a i$ and $i^\vee c j$, with inverses $p a^{-1}q^\vee$ and $q c^{-1}p^\vee$: their products are the four identities in step 3 with $D(t)=t^\vee$. This applies to the pairing of step 9. For its scalar extension use the comparison $v_{K,M}$ of [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension], rationalized at $M=\mathbf1_E$, together with $T(\mathbf1_E)\cong\mathbf1_F$ and the tensor comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. The isomorphism $T(\mathbf1_E)\cong\mathbf1_F$ is multiplication on the scalar-extended coefficient module, with inverse $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ (at integral coefficients the same identity holds levelwise for completed extension and then rationalizes). The cited internal-Hom comparison preserves evaluation, so the extended adjoints are $v_{L,\mathbf1_E}T(a)$ and $v_{K,\mathbf1_E}T(c)$ after the unit identification; their inverses are $T(a^{-1})v_{L,\mathbf1_E}^{-1}$ and $T(c^{-1})v_{K,\mathbf1_E}^{-1}$. Applying $T$ to their inverses proves they stay isomorphisms, and applying it to the splitting equations proves the same assertion on retracts. A finite sum of coefficient units extends to the same finite sum of units, and an existing retract extends by the maps $T(i),T(p)$; bounded projective local models therefore remain bounded projective local models. This is the tensor dual to the unit. The earlier Verdier evaluation has target $\omega_{X,E}$, so none of these statements identifies every constructible object with a site-perfect one.
